title: Micro-jitter attributor for token execution paths (KV-prefetch delta + streaming-aware traces)
creator: Priya Narang
description: Background: We need a higher-fidelity attribution pipeline that explains small, per-token latency and cost deltas seen across streaming and batched requests. Existing request-level traces and sampled token probes show aggregate effects, but do not reliably separate kernel scheduling/jitter, batching-induced tail latency, and KV cache prefetch/hit/miss deltas for each emitted token. This ticket designs and implements a 'micro-jitter attributor' that emits sub-token-level spans/metrics, computes cache-delta crediting, and feeds rollup aggregations for dashboards and billing reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits per-token spans with standardized attributes (token_index, seq_len, batch_id, runner_id, model_variant, cache_hit:true|false, kv_latency_ms, scheduling_delay_ms, emission_phase)
Tracing system ingests spans and joins them to request-level trace_id; we can query per-token histograms and compute mean/95/99 latency with and without cache hits
Aggregation job produces daily 'token-cost-delta' metric per model_variant and route used by Console cost breakdowns
Streaming requests are handled: tokens emitted before request completion are properly attributed to prefix cache and not double-counted
Dashboard widgets (per-route and per-model) surface token-level latency contribution, cache hit ratio, and estimated micro-cost per token
End-to-end tests validate synthetic scenarios (100% cache hit, 0% cache hit, high batching jitter) and alerts trigger if attribution deviates >15% vs ground truth in test harness
implementation_notes: Span schema: name = 'token.emit'; attributes: token_index (int), token_text_hash (low-cardinality hash), seq_len, batch_id, batch_size, runner_id, model_variant, cache_hit (bool), kv_latency_ms (float), scheduling_delay_ms (float), emission_phase ("generate"|"stream"|"prefetch"), trace_source ("host"|"edge"), sampling_reason
Emit lightweight metric events for high-cardinality fields: use coarse bucketing for kv_latency_ms and scheduling_delay_ms to avoid cardinality blowup
Sampling: 1% full-detail traces (token_text_hash populated), 5% enriched spans with token_index + cache_hit, fallback 100% with minimal numeric attributes only

Runtime change: instrument scheduler hook to record scheduling delay (timestamp when token became runnable -> timestamp when execution started); hook also records whether prefetch reserved KV entry was used
Exporter: OTLP batcher config to tag token spans with request.route and customer_id for rollups; add non-blocking retry to avoid tail amplification

Aggregation: new nightly Spark job (or Druid rollup) that ingests traces and computes token-level metrics grouped by model_variant, route, and customer tier; stores outputs in observability-timeseries for Console

Billing: prototype mapping to per-token micro-cost uses configurable weight table (kernel_ms * kernel_weight + kv_ms * kv_weight + scheduling_ms * sched_weight); weights stored in runtime-config service for fast iteration
Backwards compatibility: graceful degrade when attributes missing (treat as unknown, counted in 'unattributed' bucket)
Cardinality controls: token_text_hash is 8-char base62, only stored on full-sample; ensure PII-safe hashing and truncation
risk_mitigation: High-cardinality explosion: limit full-text hashing to 1% sample and use deterministic hashing with salt rotation policy
Telemetry volume: add dynamic sampling controlled by runtime feature flag and per-customer throttles to avoid egress storms
SDK/backpressure: ensure exporter uses non-blocking buffered queues and drops low-priority telemetry under memory pressure
Billing skew: run shadow-cost job for 2 weeks and compare to current billing model before switching production cost attribution
testing_plan: Unit tests for scheduler hook: synthetic timers and mocked KV responses to assert scheduling_delay_ms and cache_hit values
Integration test: local inference cluster run with deterministic model producing known tokens; assert per-token spans emitted and ingestion pipeline receives expected counts
Load test: replay 1M tokens/min with 20% streaming and 80% batched traffic to validate ingestion throughput and sampling knobs
E2E validation: produce 3 scenarios (full-hit, full-miss, mixed) and compare aggregation outputs to ground-truth trace replay within 5%
Dashboard sanity checks and alert rules validated in staging; incident runbook drafted
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (flagged, 0%): Ship runtime hooks behind feature flag and unit tests
Phase 1 (5% traffic): Enable enriched sampling for internal customers + telemetry ingestion; monitor volume and SLO impact
Phase 2 (25% traffic): Enable additional attributes (kv_latency_ms buckets) and run nightly aggregation in shadow mode
Phase 3 (100%): Flip default sampling to production config and enable Console dashboards; run billing reconciliation and announce change
